claims.text: The initial Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni eutectic alloy has an fcc/B2 lamellar microstructure with approximately 2 μm inter-lamellar spacing.
The approximately 2 μm initial lamellar structure is coarse.
The initial alloy exhibits catastrophic interfacial cracking and low ductility during room-temperature uniaxial tension.
Severe cold rolling followed by low-temperature annealing will transform the alloy into a patterned ultrafine lamellar configuration with coherent interfaces.
Cold rolling by more than 75% will induce high dislocation density and refine the lamellar spacing in the Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni alloy.
Annealing at 900 °C for 5 minutes will stabilize the refined Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni structure without coarsening.
An annealing window of 650–900 °C will preserve precipitate stability and interface coherence.
Room-temperature tensile testing at approximately 10^-3 s^-1 is applicable to this Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni alloy.
The treatment will produce ultrafine lamellar boundaries narrower than 100 nm.
Coherent precipitate interfaces will facilitate dislocation transmission and shear rather than crack initiation.
Refining alternating soft fcc and hard B2 lamellae will increase dislocation storage and pinning.
The post-deformation anneal will form coherent interfaces analogous to the coherent precipitate structures in the W-Ni-Fe-Ta refractory alloy.
Coherent interfaces will relieve phase-boundary stress concentrations and prevent premature crack initiation.
The treated alloy will achieve ultimate tensile strength above 1.2 GPa and elongation above 15% at room temperature.
The treatment will shift failure from interfacial cracking to uniform plastic deformation with high strain hardening.
The as-cast alloy has a fracture stress of approximately 944 MPa and elongation of approximately 25.6% at room temperature.
Failure of the as-cast alloy is dominated by stress concentration at phase interfaces.
Annealing above approximately 900 °C will coarsen the lamellae or dissolve coherent precipitates and restore brittle behavior.
A thickness reduction below 50% will be insufficient to refine the lamellae enough to arrest cracking.
Conventional HIP at 1230 °C and 152 MPa provides a control that isolates the effect of extreme pressure from the proposed treatment.

contradictions.description: The initial state is characterized as having low ductility, while the baseline assigns it approximately 25.6% elongation, which is substantial tensile ductility.
The proposed elongation target of greater than 15% does not by itself maintain or improve upon the stated 25.6% baseline elongation.
The rule treats only elongation below 10% as no improvement, although any result below the stated 25.6% baseline would represent reduced ductility.
